name: @db-ux/mcp-server

tools.name: list_components
tools.description: Returns all available DB UX component names by scanning packages/components/src/components.

tools.name: get_component_details
tools.description: Returns the list of examples (e.g. Density, Variant) for a component by reading its showcase file.

tools.name: get_component_props
tools.description: Returns the raw TypeScript content of a component's model.ts, listing all interfaces and props.

tools.name: list_design_token_categories
tools.description: Returns all available DB UX design token categories (e.g. colors, spacing, typography).

tools.name: get_design_tokens
tools.description: Returns CSS custom properties (--db-*) for a given design token category. For spacing, elevation, and density, returns compiled primitive values (rem, px, box-shadow). For colors, typography, animation, and transitions, returns SCSS variable declarations.

category.description: Token category, e.g. 'colors', 'spacing', 'typography', 'elevation', 'density'. Use list_design_token_categories to get available categories.

tools.name: list_icons
tools.description: Returns all available DB UX icon names (e.g. 'arrow_down', 'chevron_right') from the generated all-icons.ts in packages/foundations/src.

tools.name: get_example_code
tools.description: Returns the generated framework-specific source code for a component example. For Angular, the template is inline inside the @Component decorator within the .ts file. Plain HTML has no generated examples - use docs_search with docType "HTML" for that.

exampleName.description: Readable example name, e.g. 'Show Icon Leading'

tools.name: docs_search
tools.description: Searches the DB UX component and foundation documentation (guidelines, Accessibility, framework-specific docs). Only docs from packages/components/ and packages/foundations/docs/ are included. For migration guides, use list_migration_guides and get_migration_guide instead.

query.description: Search term (e.g., 'focus state', 'migration', 'accessibility'). Use empty string if you just want to read a specific component doc.

docType.description: Optional: The specific doc file to read for a component (e.g., 'Accessibility'). For migration docs, use list_migration_guides / get_migration_guide instead.

tools.name: list_migration_guides
tools.description: Returns all available DB UX migration guide names. Call this first to discover which guides exist before calling get_migration_guide.

tools.name: get_migration_guide
tools.description: Returns the full markdown content of a specific DB UX migration guide. Use this to learn the exact syntax changes needed to refactor legacy "DB UI" code to "DB UX" code.

guideName.description: Exact guide name as returned by list_migration_guides, e.g. 'color-migration' or 'icon-migration'.

tools.name: verify_migrated_code
tools.description: IMPORTANT: ALWAYS call this tool after generating or modifying Generation 3 code and BEFORE showing it to the user. The tool instructs you to verify the workspace using the project's own scripts (typecheck, lint, build) from package.json. If errors are found, fix the code and call the tool again (max 3 attempts).

tools.name: scan_generation_2_migration
tools.description: IMPORTANT: Call this tool FIRST when asked to migrate a file. Scans a source file for DB UX Design System – Generation 2 patterns (Generation 2 CSS classes (cmp-*, elm-*, rea-*) and Generation 2 Web Components (<db-*), color tokens like db-color-*, and legacy icon names) and returns a JSON report with exact line numbers and deterministic migration suggestions resolved from the official migration guides. This gives you a precise migration plan before you start generating code — no guessing needed.

filePath.description: Absolute path or path relative to the workspace root of the file to scan.

tools.name: list_visuals
tools.description: Returns all available visual reference names (e.g. dashboard, form, table). Call this first to discover which visuals exist before requesting one.

tools.name: get_visual_reference
tools.description: Returns a pre-optimised visual reference image (max 800×800 px, JPEG q75) as a Base64-encoded image block. Use this when you need visual context for complex layouts, z-index reasoning, or verifying visual hierarchies. Call list_visuals first to see available names.

name.description: Name of the visual reference (e.g. 'dashboard', 'form', 'table'). Call list_visuals to see all available names.
